lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The experience section is not ordered newest first.
items.because: The August 2022–July 2024 role appears above the October 2024–May 2025 role, delaying the more recent machine-learning experience.

items.says: Education appears before the more relevant experience and project sections.
items.because: Leading with education delays the strongest evidence of current technical scope and impact.

items.says: The duty framing does not identify the technical work performed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the dashboards were built, redesigned, instrumented, or merely administered.

items.says: The dashboard ownership claim gives no operational result.
“Load tests that fail the build” shifts to present tense in an ended role.
“Maintained the CI pipeline” buries the stronger release-cycle result behind routine responsibility.
items.because: A scanning reader registers maintenance before the reduction from two weeks to three days.

items.says: “Automated regression checks” does not identify the model property or release risk being tested.
The backlog result is buried and attached ambiguously to several preceding actions.
items.because: The reader reaches the result only after several activities, and “which” could refer to the migration or their combination.

items.says: Logging, onboarding, and on-call details overload the migration bullet.
items.because: They compete with the migration and backlog result and leave the reader unsure which work belongs together.

items.says: The strongest Eastern Robotics bullet is not placed first.
items.because: The 30-service migration and dispatch outcome establish technical ownership more quickly than the dashboard line.

items.says: “ML-extracted features” does not identify the model or feature-extraction technique used.
Dynamic batching cannot explain a latency reduction for truly single-request edge inference.
items.because: At concurrency one, there are no other requests to combine, and batching may add delay.

items.says: The method-heavy opening buries the 5% latency reduction.
items.because: A scanning reader encounters the methods and acronyms before learning what changed.

items.says: “GRPO” and “SFT” are not expanded on first use.
A single scored rollout per prompt cannot stabilize standard GRPO and conflicts with the preceding grouped-rollouts claim.
items.because: Standard GRPO needs multiple scored rollouts for a nonzero group-relative advantage.

items.says: “Stabilised GRPO training” gives no measurable definition of stability.
The single-rollout wording repeats the same one-trajectory idea.
“AI-first engineering practices” is undefined jargon that does not identify the work introduced.
items.because: A technical reader cannot determine what was implemented or what multi-agent expertise it demonstrates.

items.says: The claimed delivery and downstream-team benefits lack a checkable result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what became faster, what improved, or whether downstream teams adopted the change.

items.says: “A 50% reduction” is mathematically wrong for a decrease from 900 ms to 600 ms.
items.because: A 300 ms decrease against a 900 ms baseline is 33.3%.

items.says: “By 12%” incorrectly describes the change from 71% to 83%.
items.because: The absolute change is 12 percentage points, while the relative increase is approximately 16.9%.

items.says: The strongest Agent Runtime Suite bullet is not placed first.
items.because: The task-completion line gives the clearest product-quality result, baseline, and multi-agent intervention.

items.says: “The benchmark suite” does not identify the tasks or workload represented by the completion rate.
“Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics” does not identify the technical work that enabled the contribution.
“A Kendall correlation of 0.89” does not name the two rankings or variables being correlated.
“Showed” is less precise than the experimental action described.
“Their modules with layered instrumentation” leaves the responsible modules and diagnostic method unspecified.
“Each was fixed upstream” uses passive voice and hides who fixed the defects.
